## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. ## How to run it

<sub>[context source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.12950v3): Context length from the maker's technical report.</sub>

<pre>
download                       size  score
4-bit q4_k_m               ~20.72GB   39.9
8-bit q8_0                 ~40.94GB   39.9
4-bit Q4_K_M                ~20.2GB   39.9
8-bit Q8_0                  ~35.9GB   39.9
4-bit mlx-4bit · mac only   ~19.4GB   39.9
</pre>

<sub>The score is the published model's; quantized downloads haven't been evaluated separately.</sub>

### Run it on your own machine

**llama.cpp** · install: macOS / Linux `curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh` · Windows `irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex` · [other ways](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/install.md) · Homebrew and winget installs name the commands llama-cli and llama-server instead.

```sh
# 4-bit Q4_K_M · ~20.2GB
llama cli -hf mradermacher/CodeLlama-34b-Instruct-hf-GGUF:Q4_K_M
# or start a local server and open the address it prints (http://localhost:9931)
llama serve -hf mradermacher/CodeLlama-34b-Instruct-hf-GGUF:Q4_K_M
# 8-bit Q8_0 · ~35.9GB
llama cli -hf mradermacher/CodeLlama-34b-Instruct-hf-GGUF:Q8_0
# or start a local server and open the address it prints (http://localhost:9931)
llama serve -hf mradermacher/CodeLlama-34b-Instruct-hf-GGUF:Q8_0
```

**LM Studio** · install: [macOS / Windows / Linux](https://lmstudio.ai/download) · Open the app once before using the lms command.

```sh
# 4-bit Q4_K_M · ~20.2GB
lms get https://huggingface.co/mradermacher/CodeLlama-34b-Instruct-hf-GGUF@Q4_K_M -y
# then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name
# 8-bit Q8_0 · ~35.9GB
lms get https://huggingface.co/mradermacher/CodeLlama-34b-Instruct-hf-GGUF@Q8_0 -y
# then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name
# 4-bit mlx-4bit · mac only · ~19.4GB
lms get https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/CodeLlama-34b-Instruct-hf-4bit -y
# then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name
```

**Ollama** · install: [macOS / Windows](https://ollama.com/download) · Linux `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh`

```sh
# 4-bit q4_k_m · ~20.72GB
ollama run codellama:34b-instruct-q4_K_M
# 8-bit q8_0 · ~40.94GB
ollama run codellama:34b-instruct-q8_0
# 4-bit Q4_K_M · ~20.2GB
ollama run hf.co/mradermacher/CodeLlama-34b-Instruct-hf-GGUF:Q4_K_M
# 8-bit Q8_0 · ~35.9GB
ollama run hf.co/mradermacher/CodeLlama-34b-Instruct-hf-GGUF:Q8_0
```

**MLX (Mac)** · install: with uv `uv tool install mlx-lm` · or `pip install mlx-lm` · Apple silicon Macs only, text only.

```sh
# 4-bit mlx-4bit · mac only · ~19.4GB
mlx_lm.chat --model mlx-community/CodeLlama-34b-Instruct-hf-4bit
# or start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://localhost:8080/v1
mlx_lm.server --model mlx-community/CodeLlama-34b-Instruct-hf-4bit
```
